title: America’s Best Answer to the China-Russia Alliance
gist: Hamilton and Stent argue the 'reverse Nixon' bid to split Russia from China has failed, but the partnership is lopsided, transactional and full of frictions over energy, Central Asia, the Arctic and Africa. Washington should raise the alliance's operating costs via secondary tariffs on Russian energy buyers, exploiting mutual distrust, and rebuilding 'allied scale' across Europe and Asia.

insights.claim: The Trump administration's early second-term 'reverse Nixon' strategy to pry Russia away from China failed, and Trump's tariffs, sanctions and war against Iran have pushed Russia and China even closer together.
insights.speaker: Daniel S. Hamilton, Angela Stent
insights.so_what: US coercive policy is consolidating the Russia-China bloc rather than fragmenting it.
insights.quote: In fact, Trump’s tariffs, sanctions, and war against Iran have pushed Russia and China even closer together.

insights.claim: Washington should avoid the false choice between a grand realignment with Russia and passively accepting a solidified China-Russia partnership, and instead aim to make the relationship more costly and difficult to operate.
insights.speaker: Daniel S. Hamilton, Angela Stent
insights.so_what: Signals a policy direction of incremental pressure (sanctions, tariffs, alliance-building) rather than detente with Moscow.

insights.claim: Despite mutual distrust, Russian and Chinese leaders carefully manage their differences and red lines, so no reverse Nixon option currently exists; even an FSB report calling China 'the enemy' told officers to avoid harming bilateral relations.

insights.so_what: Russian destabilization threatens Chinese commercial interests in African resource economies.

insights.claim: Russia and China have linked Indo-Pacific and North Atlantic security through joint exercises and patrols, and US allies admit they are not prepared for simultaneous conflicts in East Asia and Europe.

insights.claim: Trump administration efforts to confine Europe's strategic focus to its own continent and Asian allies to their region weaken both alliances by signaling that US commitments are limited and conditional.

insights.so_what: Perceived conditional US commitments push allies toward hedging and self-reliant defense spending.
